source: BK5 printed p.2 = book5-6.pdf PDF p.8; ER-28; Step 7 speculative derivation from topology
note: Speculative (Step 7): every expect is derived by hand from the five wires and the p.2 rule (either slide switch turns light 1 on or off whatever the other's position; ER-28: each move flips the light). Topology: 1+/1A feeds light 1, 1B/1V feeds slide switch 1 set-2 arm; switch 1 LEFT (travel 0) closes V-U, RIGHT (travel 1000) closes V-W; 1U/2U and 1W/2W cross to slide switch 2's set-2 contacts, whose arm 2V returns to 2- (2V/2-). Light 1 is lit exactly when both switches are on the same side: LL and RR ON, LR and RL OFF. This is the inverse of the page's worked LEFT/RIGHT example (manual defect O-C24, independent of switch polarity), which is not asserted. The script starts from the page example's switch 2 RIGHT with switch 1 RIGHT, makes the page's two moves (switch 1 LEFT, then switch 2 LEFT), then moves each switch back, so all four positions and two flips per switch are checked. The 500 ms advance before each expect lets the lamp finish its thermal transient; the page states no timing.

script.cite: BK5 printed p.2 = book5-6.pdf PDF p.8, stated rule: the light can be turned on or off from either slide switch regardless of the other's position (ER-28 = errata.pdf PDF p.3: moving either slide switch changes the light to the opposite state); derived from topology (absolute phase not printed reliably, O-C24): both RIGHT (RR). 1+/1A feeds light 1; 1B/1V feeds switch 1 set-2 arm, which RIGHT closes to 1W; 1W/2W; switch 2 arm 2V RIGHT closes to 2W, and 2V/2- returns: light 1 lit
script.quote: Regardless of which position the switch is in, the switch at the other location can always turn the light either on or off.
